title: Geometric inbuf growth instead of reallocate-per-write
description: inbuf_append now uses geometric doubling (cap*2) instead of kmalloc(old_len+new_len) per append. For large keys (ML-DSA-87: 4896 bytes written in multiple write() calls), the old approach was O(n) allocations. The new approach is O(log n) allocations. A well-intentioned contributor reading the old code might simplify this back to krealloc or per-write allocation on the grounds that keys are small and written once. Defense: the write()-before-ioctl pattern is used for DO_KDF input too (PBKDF2 passwords, HKDF IKM), where streaming writes are more natural and reducing allocations matters for key material (each freed buffer requires memzero_explicit before free, so fewer allocations = fewer zeroize operations = less overhead).
close_reason: Decision records — no code change needed
